answer: Proof of space counters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit dedicated storage to cryptographic tables. When peers whisper timed challenges, the agent must return sector proofs, ensuring an attacker cannot mirror one allocation across cloned nodes. The verifiable cost per identity is dedicating raw physical sectors on ferrous platters. A key limitation is that time-memory trade-offs allow fast processors to recompute proofs dynamically rather than storing them.
